questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Bills was passed by the 17th Lok Sabha of India on 17 December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**129th Constitutional Amendment Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **129th Constitutional Amendment Bill** was passed by the **17th Lok Sabha** of India on **17 December 2024**. This bill is significant in the constitutional history of India.
 
• This amendment primarily aimed at **strengthening cooperative federalism** by enhancing the powers of states and providing clarity regarding certain matters of jurisdiction.
 
• The bill was introduced to **address socio-political and administrative issues** concerning governance and federal structure in India.
 
• The **17th Lok Sabha**, elected in 2019, has been active in passing various progressive bills, including the **129th Amendment**, which was one of the landmark decisions of this period.
 
• **Constitutional amendments** require a special majority in Parliament, and this bill successfully garnered the required support, showcasing the commitment of lawmakers toward national progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Amendments in India:**

 
 
• Under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution, Parliament has the power to amend the Constitution.
 
• Amendments can be classified into three types: **Simple majority amendments**, **Special majority amendments**, and those requiring **ratification by states**.
 
• India has witnessed several landmark amendments, such as the **42nd Amendment (1976)**, which is considered the most comprehensive and controversial amendment.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lok Sabha in Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha plays a crucial role in passing constitutional amendment bills. A **two-thirds majority** of members present and voting is required for the approval of such bills.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha debate the provisions of the amendment extensively before casting their votes.
 
• After Lok Sabha approval, the bill is sent to the Rajya Sabha for deliberation and voting.
 
 
 
• **17th Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The 17th Lok Sabha was constituted following the **2019 General Elections**, with the Bharatiya Janata Party securing a majority.
 
• It has been instrumental in passing several key legislations, including the **Citizenship Amendment Act (2019)** and the **129th Constitutional Amendment Bill**.
 
• The 17th Lok Sabha is noted for its focus on governance reforms and social welfare schemes.
 
 
 
• **Process of Constitutional Amendment:**
 
 
• An amendment can be introduced in either House of Parliament as a bill.
 
• It must be passed by both Houses with a **special majority**.
 
• In cases involving federal issues, amendments also require the **ratification by half of the state legislatures**.
 
• Once all procedures are completed, the amendment is notified by the President of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Considerations:**

 
 
• Constitutional amendments cannot alter the **basic structure** of the Constitution, as ruled by the Supreme Court in the **Keshavananda Bharati Case (1973)**.
 
• The **President of India** plays a ceremonial role in signing the amendment bill into law after parliamentary approval.
 
 
 
• **Historical Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• **1st Amendment (1951):** Added restrictions to freedom of speech and expression.
 
• **42nd Amendment (1976):** Introduced the term “**Socialist**” and “**Secular**” in the Preamble.
 
• **73rd and 74th Amendments (1992):** Strengthened **local self-governance** through Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 129th Amendment:**
 
 
• It reflects the evolving needs of India's governance framework.
 
• Focuses on addressing **administrative concerns** and **state-specific issues**.
 
• Strengthens the federal structure of India by providing clarity in jurisdictional matters.

questions.question: As of 30 April 2025, the ‘GenomeIndiaA’ project has completed whole genome sequencing (WGS) database of approximately how many individuals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10000**__.

• The **GenomeIndia Project** is an ambitious initiative launched by the Government of India to create a comprehensive database of the genetic diversity of the Indian population.
 
• As of **30 April 2025**, the project has successfully completed the whole genome sequencing (WGS) database of approximately **10,000 individuals**.
 
• The project's primary goal is to map genetic variations across different regions, communities, and ethnic groups in India to better understand genetic predispositions to diseases, traits, and health conditions.
 
• Whole genome sequencing involves analyzing the entire DNA sequence of individuals, providing insights into genetic markers, hereditary diseases, and potential therapeutic interventions.
 
• The data generated from the GenomeIndia Project will be vital for research in **personalized medicine, genomics-based healthcare solutions**, and studying the genetic impact of environmental factors.

questions.question: Which edition of SIMBEX (Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise) was held in Singapore in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**32nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SIMBEX (Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise)** is an annual maritime exercise between **India** and **Singapore**, aimed at strengthening military and naval cooperation.
 
• The **32nd edition** of SIMBEX was held in **July 2025** in **Singapore**, showcasing advanced naval capabilities and collaborative operations between the two countries.
 
• The exercise includes activities such as **anti-submarine warfare**, **maritime interdiction operations**, **surface warfare**, and **air defense exercises**.
 
• SIMBEX reflects the strategic partnership and shared commitment to maintaining maritime security in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)** and adjacent waters.
 
• The 32nd edition marked another milestone in the series, highlighting the **long-standing defense collaboration** between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SIMBEX Overview:**

 
 
• The exercise began in **1994** as a modest anti-submarine warfare drill and has evolved into a complex and advanced bilateral naval exercise.
 
• It aims to enhance interoperability and mutual understanding between the **Indian Navy** and the **Republic of Singapore Navy**.
 
• SIMBEX is a key component of the defense cooperation agreement signed between India and Singapore.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy’s Participation:**
 
 
• The Indian Navy deploys cutting-edge vessels, such as **destroyers, frigates, submarines**, and **maritime patrol aircraft**, for SIMBEX exercises.
 
• It also showcases operational capabilities in areas like **underwater warfare**, **search and rescue**, and **naval aviation**.
 
 
 
• **Republic of Singapore Navy’s Role:**
 
 
• The Republic of Singapore Navy contributes its modern fleet, including **Formidable-class frigates**, **Victory-class missile corvettes**, and **submarines**.
 
• Singapore emphasizes the importance of regional maritime security and actively engages with India through SIMBEX.
 
 
 
• **Geopolitical Significance:**
 
 
• SIMBEX enhances **regional stability** and maritime cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region, a vital area for global trade and security.
 
• It underscores the importance of maintaining **freedom of navigation**, countering **piracy**, and addressing threats like **terrorism** in maritime domains.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Milestones:**

 
 
• The first SIMBEX exercise was conducted in **1994**, focusing on anti-submarine warfare.
 
• Over the years, the scope of the exercise has expanded to include advanced maritime operations and joint naval drills.
 
 
 
• **India-Singapore Defense Partnership:**
 
 
• India and Singapore signed a defense cooperation agreement in **2003**, strengthening military ties and fostering collaboration.
 
• The partnership also includes joint air force and army exercises, apart from SIMBEX.
 
 
 
• **Key Objectives of SIMBEX:**
 
 
• Enhance **interoperability** between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy.
 
• Promote **regional maritime security** and stability in the Indian Ocean Region.
 
• Build mutual trust and understanding through joint operational training.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• Both nations aim to further deepen defense cooperation, leveraging SIMBEX to address emerging maritime security challenges.
 
• SIMBEX serves as a platform for exploring new areas of collaboration, such as **cybersecurity** and **space-based maritime surveillance**.

questions.question: Which spacecraft will be used for Axiom‑4?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Crew Dragon C213**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crew Dragon C213** is a spacecraft developed by **SpaceX** under NASA’s Commercial Crew Program. It is part of the Crew Dragon family of spacecraft used for crewed missions to the International Space Station (ISS).
 
• The spacecraft is designed for **low Earth orbit missions**, including transporting astronauts to and from the ISS. It is reusable and capable of carrying up to **seven passengers**.
 
• The Axiom-4 mission, a private crewed mission to the ISS organized by **Axiom Space**, will use Crew Dragon C213 for its transportation. This showcases the growing role of private companies in space exploration.
 
• Crew Dragon features advanced safety systems, including an **abort system** capable of propelling the spacecraft away from the rocket in case of emergencies during launch.
 
• The spacecraft has been a part of several successful missions, including NASA’s Crew-1, Crew-2, and private missions such as **Inspiration4**, demonstrating its reliability and versatility.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SpaceX and Crew Dragon:**

 
 
• **SpaceX**, founded by **Elon Musk**, is a private aerospace manufacturer and space transportation company. It aims to reduce space transportation costs and enable the colonization of Mars.
 
• The Crew Dragon spacecraft is an evolution of the Dragon 1 cargo spacecraft. It is equipped with **life support systems** and autonomous docking capabilities.
 
• It is launched aboard the **Falcon 9 rocket**, another SpaceX innovation known for its reusability.
 
 
 
• **Axiom Space and Axiom Missions:**
 
 
• **Axiom Space** is a private space infrastructure developer. It aims to build the first commercial space station, which will eventually replace the ISS.
 
• Axiom missions, such as Axiom-4, provide opportunities for private astronauts and researchers to work aboard the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Other Spacecraft in the Options:**
 
 
• **Soyuz MS-24:** A Russian spacecraft operated by Roscosmos, primarily used for transporting astronauts to and from the ISS. It is not used for Axiom-4.
 
• **Starliner:** Developed by Boeing as part of NASA’s Commercial Crew Program. It has not been selected for Axiom-4.
 
• **Orion:** A spacecraft developed by NASA for deep space exploration, including Artemis missions to the Moon. It is not designed for low Earth orbit missions like Axiom-4.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Private Space Missions:**
 
 
• Private missions like Axiom-4 represent a shift toward **commercialization of space**, enabling broader access to space exploration.
 
• They complement government-led missions, fostering innovation and reducing costs through competition.

questions.question: How many new Khelo India Centres are planned by the Delhi Government in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6 new Khelo India Centres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Delhi Government** has announced the establishment of **6 new Khelo India Centres** in 2025 to promote sports and nurture young talent in the region.
 
• The initiative is part of the **Khelo India Scheme**, a flagship program by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports aimed at **revitalizing the sports culture** in India at the grassroots level.
 
• These centres will focus on identifying and training athletes in various disciplines, ensuring access to **quality infrastructure, coaching, and resources**.
 
• The centres are expected to cater to **young athletes**, providing them with opportunities to excel in national and international competitions.
 
• They will also align with the government's commitment to enhancing **sports infrastructure** and fostering youth engagement in sports activities across Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Scheme:**

 
 
• **Launched in 2018**, the Khelo India Scheme aims to **develop sports infrastructure**, identify talent, and provide financial assistance to athletes.
 
• It covers various components such as **Talent Identification and Development**, **Sports for Women**, **Promotion of Rural and Indigenous Games**, and **Sports for Peace and Development**.
 
• The scheme also organizes the **Khelo India Youth Games** and **Khelo India University Games** to provide young athletes with a competitive platform.
 
 
 
• **Existing Sports Infrastructure in Delhi:**
 
 
• Delhi is home to several prominent sporting facilities, including the **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium**, **Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium**, and **Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium**.
 
• The establishment of new Khelo India Centres will further **enhance sports accessibility** and bridge the gap between aspiring athletes and professional training.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Khelo India Centres:**
 
 
• The centres will provide a **structured pathway** for young athletes to transition from grassroots to elite-level sports.
 
• They will also contribute to **community engagement** by encouraging local participation and fostering a culture of fitness and sportsmanship.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Government's Initiatives in Sports:**
 
 
• The Delhi Government has been actively promoting sports through initiatives like **Mission Excellence**, which provides financial support to athletes.
 
• The new Khelo India Centres will complement these efforts, ensuring a holistic approach to sports development in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Khelo India Youth Games:**

 
 
• These games are organized annually and serve as a platform for young athletes to **showcase their talent**.
 
• The games include a wide range of sporting disciplines such as athletics, archery, basketball, boxing, football, gymnastics, judo, swimming, and more.
 
• The 2023 edition of the games was hosted in **Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Sports Promotion:**
 
 
• As part of the Khelo India initiative, indigenous sports like **Kabaddi**, **Kalaripayattu**, **Kho-Kho**, and **Mallakhamb** are being promoted to preserve and popularize traditional games.
 
• This ensures the inclusivity and cultural representation of sports across India.

questions.question: Which NFL player won the BET Sportsman of the Year Award 2025?

__

• The award is presented by BET to celebrate athletes who have demonstrated exceptional skills, sportsmanship, and contributions to society.
 
• In the 2024 NFL season, Jalen Hurts showcased extraordinary leadership and skill, leading the Eagles to the playoffs and earning accolades for his performance under pressure.
 
• Hurts is known for his versatility as a quarterback, combining strong passing accuracy with the ability to execute rushing plays effectively.
 
• Off the field, Hurts has been actively involved in community service initiatives, reflecting his commitment to social causes and inspiring young athletes.

__
 
• **About Jalen Hurts:**

 
 
• Born on **August 7, 1998**, in Houston, Texas, Jalen Hurts played college football at **Alabama** and **Oklahoma**.
 
• Drafted by the Philadelphia Eagles in the second round of the **2020 NFL Draft**, Hurts quickly established himself as a rising star in the league.
 
• Hurts is celebrated for his **dual-threat quarterback capabilities**, excelling in both passing and rushing.
 
 
 
• **BET Sportsman of the Year Award:**
 
 
• Organized by **Black Entertainment Television (BET)**, this award honors athletes who excel in their respective sports and positively impact society.

• **Community Contributions:**
 
 
• Jalen Hurts is actively involved in initiatives supporting **youth education**, sports programs, and **mental health awareness**.
 
• He has partnered with organizations to provide resources and mentorship to underserved communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Other nominees for the BET Sportsman of the Year Award 2025 included **Patrick Mahomes**, **Lamar Jackson**, and **Josh Allen**, all of whom delivered commendable performances in their respective NFL seasons.
 
• While all nominees showcased remarkable skills, Jalen Hurts stood out for his combination of athletic achievement and community impact.
 
 
 
• **Notable Achievements:**
 
 
• Hurts was ranked among the **top quarterbacks** in the league for his rushing touchdowns and passing efficiency during the 2024 season.

questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the 6th BIMSTEC Summit in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thailand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **6th BIMSTEC Summit** was hosted by **Thailand** in **April 2025**. BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) is a regional organization comprising South Asian and Southeast Asian countries.
 
• **BIMSTEC** includes seven member countries: **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, and Thailand**. These nations are focused on enhancing regional cooperation across various sectors.
 
• The summit was attended by heads of states and governments of the member countries to discuss critical regional issues and strategies for economic and social progress.
 
• The theme for the 6th BIMSTEC Summit was centered around **"Towards a Resilient and Prosperous Bay of Bengal Region."** Thailand, as the host country, emphasized enhancing collaboration in areas such as trade, connectivity, technology, and disaster management.
 
• Hosting this summit showcased Thailand's commitment to strengthening regional cooperation and its strategic role as a key player in the BIMSTEC framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About BIMSTEC:**

 
 
• The **Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC)** was established in **1997** with the aim of fostering regional integration and cooperation among member states.
 
• BIMSTEC focuses on 14 priority sectors, including **trade, technology, energy, transport, fisheries, agriculture, public health, poverty alleviation, counter-terrorism, and environment**.
 
• The BIMSTEC Secretariat is located in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**.
 
 
 
• **Thailand's Role in BIMSTEC:**
 
 
• Thailand plays a critical role in BIMSTEC due to its geographical position, connecting South Asia with Southeast Asia.
 
• The country has been actively involved in promoting **connectivity projects**, including the development of the **Trilateral Highway** between India, Myanmar, and Thailand.
 
• Thailand has also emphasized enhancing maritime cooperation and disaster management mechanisms within the BIMSTEC framework.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the BIMSTEC Summit:**
 
 
• BIMSTEC summits provide a platform for high-level discussions on regional issues, fostering collaboration among member countries to address common challenges.
 
• The summits aim to enhance economic growth, strengthen connectivity, and promote sustainable development in the Bay of Bengal region.
 
• The organization serves as a bridge between South Asia and Southeast Asia, boosting trade and cultural exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Key Outcomes of Previous Summits:**
 
 
• The 5th BIMSTEC Summit, held in **Colombo, Sri Lanka**, focused on the adoption of the **BIMSTEC Charter** and agreements on enhancing connectivity and counter-terrorism cooperation.
 
• Member states have consistently worked towards implementing the **Master Plan for Transport Connectivity (2018-2030)** to improve regional connectivity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thailand's Strategic Importance:**

 
 
• Thailand is strategically located in Southeast Asia, serving as a gateway between South Asia and ASEAN countries.
 
• The country has been a strong advocate for regional integration and has actively participated in BIMSTEC initiatives.
 
 
 
• **BIMSTEC and Regional Connectivity:**
 
 
• BIMSTEC has been working on enhancing connectivity through projects like the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway** and the **Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project**.
 
• These projects aim to improve trade links and transportation infrastructure across the region.
 
 
 
• **Future Prospects:**
 
 
• BIMSTEC aims to expand its cooperation in areas such as **blue economy, climate change adaptation,** and **people-to-people connectivity**.
 
• The organization seeks to strengthen ties with other regional and global entities to address emerging challenges and opportunities.

questions.question: As per the Economic Survey, 2024–25, which mission is part of India’s Space Vision, 2047, for human spaceflight?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaganyaan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gaganyaan** is India's first human spaceflight mission under the ambitious **India's Space Vision, 2047**.
 
• The mission was announced by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on **August 15, 2018**, during his Independence Day speech.
 
• **Gaganyaan** aims to send a crew of **three astronauts** into low Earth orbit for a period of **up to seven days**.
 
• This mission is being developed under the leadership of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, with significant advancements in space technology and infrastructure.
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024–25** highlighted Gaganyaan as a key milestone in India's space exploration strategy, contributing to technological innovation and national pride.
 
• **Unmanned mission tests** for Gaganyaan are being conducted to ensure the safety and reliability of the crewed flight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India's Space Vision, 2047:**

 
 
• A long-term strategic plan by **ISRO** to position India as a global leader in space exploration and technological development.
 
• Focuses on **human spaceflight, interplanetary missions, space station establishment**, and advancements in satellite communication.
 
• Includes missions like **Gaganyaan, Chandrayaan-3, Aditya-L1**, and future Mars exploration missions.
 
 
 
• **Gaganyaan Mission Features:**
 
 
• The spacecraft consists of an **orbital module** that houses a crew module and a service module.
 
• The crew module is equipped with **life-support systems** and environmental controls to ensure astronaut safety.
 
• ISRO plans to collaborate with international space agencies like **NASA, Roscosmos**, and the European Space Agency (ESA) for technological support.
 
• The mission will use the **GSLV Mk III rocket**, which is India's most powerful launch vehicle.
 
 
 
• **Training of Astronauts:**
 
 
• Indian astronauts, referred to as **Vyomanauts**, are undergoing specialized training for spaceflight in collaboration with **Russia**.
 
• The training includes simulations of zero-gravity conditions, survival techniques, and spacecraft operations.
 
 
 
• **Other Missions Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Vikram:** Refers to the **Vikram lander** used in Chandrayaan missions for lunar exploration. It is not a human spaceflight mission.
 
• **Samudrayaan:** A project for deep-sea exploration under the Ministry of Earth Sciences. It focuses on ocean resources and is unrelated to spaceflight.
 
• **Mangalyaan:** Also known as the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM), launched in **2013**, aimed at studying Mars. It is an interplanetary mission and not a human spaceflight mission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gaganyaan Budget:** The mission has an estimated cost of **₹10,000 crore**, making it one of India's most expensive space projects.
 
• **ISRO's Achievements:** Gaganyaan marks a significant milestone in ISRO's journey, which has included missions like **Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan**, and **PSLV launches**.
 
• **Global Impact:** Successful execution of Gaganyaan would position India as the **fourth nation** to achieve human spaceflight capability after the **USA, Russia**, and **China**.
 
• **Technological Innovations:** The mission will drive advancements in **aerospace engineering, robotics, life-support systems**, and **space medicine**.
 
• **Future Plans:** Following Gaganyaan, ISRO plans to explore **space station development** and interplanetary human missions.

questions.question: As per Sustainable Development Goals – National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, the percentage of population using an improved drinking water source in rural areas increased from 94.57% in 2015-16 to what percentage in 2024-25, indicating significant progress toward universal safe water access in rural India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.9962**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** aim to ensure universal access to safe drinking water by **2030**, as part of Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation).
 
• According to the **National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report 2025**, the percentage of the population in rural areas using improved drinking water sources increased from **94.57%** in **2015-16** to **99.62%** in **2024-25**.
 
• Improved drinking water sources include **piped water supply, borewells, protected springs, and rainwater collection systems**, ensuring safe and reliable access.
 
• This progress highlights India's commitment to achieving the SDGs by addressing rural water challenges through programs such as the **Jal Jeevan Mission**.
 
• The increase from **94.57%** to **99.62%** represents a significant improvement, nearing universal access to safe drinking water in rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6):**

 
 
• It aims to ensure the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all by **2030**.
 
• Key targets include achieving universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water, improving water quality, and ensuring integrated water resource management.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission:**
 
 
• Launched in **2019**, this government initiative aims to provide functional household tap connections (FHTC) to every rural household by **2024**.
 
• It focuses on ensuring safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections and strengthening water resource management.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):**
 
 
• The NIF is a framework developed by the Indian government to monitor progress on the SDGs at the national and sub-national levels.
 
• It consists of a set of indicators aligned with the SDGs to track India's performance and highlight areas needing improvement.
 
 
 
• **Improved Drinking Water Sources:**
 
 
• These include piped water on premises, public taps, tube wells, boreholes, protected dug wells, protected springs, and rainwater collection systems.
 
• Such sources are less likely to be contaminated and are considered reliable for safe drinking water.

questions.question: Which among the community-focused transparency initiatives did the Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh police introduce in September 2025?

options.text: Police Outreach Day' to resolve neighborhood safety concerns

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Vadi Samvad Diwas** was introduced by the **Ghaziabad Police, Uttar Pradesh**, in **September 2025** as a community-focused transparency initiative aimed at building trust between citizens and the police.
 
• The initiative allows citizens to engage directly with **investigators** to discuss and resolve their cases transparently and effectively.
 
• This program ensures **accessibility** and **accountability** in investigations by providing a platform for individuals to interact with police officials face-to-face.
 
• The initiative specifically focuses on **case updates**, addressing public grievances, and ensuring citizens' concerns are heard without bureaucratic hurdles.

• This initiative involves organizing community events where citizens can discuss **neighborhood safety concerns** and seek solutions collaboratively with local law enforcement.
 
• While it aims to improve community relations, it does not focus on individual case updates or direct investigator interaction, unlike **Vadi Samvad Diwas**.

• This involves the release of **monthly action reports** by the police to keep the public informed about their activities and performance.
 
• It enhances transparency at a macro level, but it does not provide a platform for personal engagement or case-specific discussions with investigators.
 
 
 
• **Jan Sunwai Sabha**:
 
 
• This program allows direct interaction between citizens and police officers to address **grievances** and discuss broader issues affecting public safety.

• **Trust Building:** Initiatives fostering direct dialogue between citizens and investigators reduce instances of mistrust and encourage **collaborative problem-solving**.

questions.question: As of March 2025, what percentage of India's area is earthquake-prone?

__
 
• **India's seismic zone classification:** India is divided into four seismic zones (Zone II, III, IV, and V) based on earthquake risk. Zone V is the most earthquake-prone, while Zone II is the least.
 
• **Percentage of earthquake-prone areas:** As per the latest data available until **March 2025**, approximately **0.59%** of India's total geographical area is classified as highly earthquake-prone (Zone V).
 
• **Regions under Zone V:** The areas in Zone V include parts of northeastern India, the Himalayan region, and areas in western and central India that are prone to frequent seismic activity.
 
• **Historical earthquakes:** India has experienced devastating earthquakes such as the **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, the **Uttarkashi earthquake (1991)**, and the **Kashmir earthquake (2005)**, highlighting the importance of seismic monitoring.
 
• **Government initiatives:** The Government of India has implemented various measures, such as the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, to enhance earthquake preparedness and minimize risks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seismic Zones in India:**

 
 
• **Zone II:** Least active zone covering areas with minimal seismic activity.
 
• **Zone III:** Moderately active zone including parts of central India and the Gangetic plains.
 
• **Zone IV:** High-risk areas such as Delhi, parts of Punjab, and some Himalayan regions.
 
• **Zone V:** Extremely high-risk areas such as northeastern India, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and parts of Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):** Established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, NDMA focuses on disaster preparedness, mitigation, and response strategies.
 
• **Causes of Earthquakes:** Earthquakes are caused by tectonic plate movements, volcanic eruptions, and human activities such as mining or reservoir-induced seismicity.
 
• **Impact of Earthquakes:** Earthquakes can lead to loss of lives, destruction of infrastructure, and displacement of communities, necessitating effective disaster management practices.
 
• **Building Codes:** The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has developed seismic design codes to ensure buildings are resistant to earthquake forces.

• **Earthquake Magnitude Scale:** Earthquakes are measured using the **Richter scale**, which quantifies the amount of energy released during a seismic event.
 
• **Government Policies:** The Government has launched initiatives like the **National Earthquake Risk Mitigation Project (NERMP)** to reduce vulnerabilities.
 
• **Public Awareness:** Regular public awareness campaigns are conducted to educate citizens on earthquake safety measures.
 
• **Global Collaboration:** India collaborates with international organizations for seismic research and disaster management, such as the **UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)**.

questions.question: On 29 June 2025, the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change issued Model Rules to streamline regulations for _______________.

options.text: interest rates of loans for farmers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tree felling in agricultural lands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change issued **Model Rules** on **29 June 2025** to regulate and streamline **tree felling in agricultural lands**. This aims to ensure sustainable use of resources and protect environmental balance. 
 
• Tree felling in agricultural lands is a critical activity that requires proper regulation, as it impacts **biodiversity, soil health, and carbon sequestration**.
 
• The Model Rules aim to simplify the **procedural requirements** for farmers and landowners while maintaining compliance with **environmental norms** and forest laws. 
 
• The regulations are essential to prevent **indiscriminate deforestation**, encourage sustainable agricultural practices, and ensure that farmers comply with national and international environmental standards. 
 
• The rules provide clarity on the types of trees that can be felled, the **permissions required**, and the **replanting obligations** to mitigate the ecological impact. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Impact of Tree Felling on Agriculture:**

 
 
• **Soil Erosion:** Trees play a crucial role in preventing soil erosion. Their removal can lead to the loss of fertile topsoil, negatively affecting agricultural productivity.
 
• **Biodiversity Loss:** Trees provide shelter and food for various organisms. Indiscriminate tree felling disrupts ecosystems, leading to biodiversity loss.
 
• **Carbon Sequestration:** Trees absorb carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Their removal reduces the land's ability to sequester carbon.
 
• **Microclimate Regulation:** Trees influence local weather patterns, including temperature and humidity levels. Removing them can make agricultural lands less favorable for farming.
 
 
 
• **Regulations and Permissions for Tree Felling:**
 
 
• Under the **Indian Forest Act, 1927**, and various state-specific laws, tree felling often requires prior approval from forest departments.
 
• Farmers may need to follow specific procedures, including obtaining a **tree-felling permit**, documenting the purpose, and complying with replanting norms.
 
• Some states provide exemptions for certain species, such as **subabul** and **eucalyptus**, which are grown primarily for commercial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Tree Management Practices:**
 
 
• **Agroforestry:** Farmers can integrate trees into agricultural systems to balance production with ecological conservation.
 
• **Selective Logging:** Instead of clear-cutting, selective logging preserves the overall ecological balance while allowing resource use.
 
• **Replanting Mandates:** Governments often require replanting trees to ensure sustainability and compensate for the ecological loss.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• **National Agroforestry Policy, 2014:** Encourages the integration of trees into agricultural landscapes for ecological and economic benefits.
 
• **Compensatory Afforestation Programme:** Mandates replanting trees in designated areas to offset deforestation impacts.
 
• **Green India Mission:** Aims to restore degraded ecosystems, enhance tree cover, and combat climate change.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **State-Specific Rules:** Different states in India have varying rules for tree felling. For example, Maharashtra and Karnataka have specific guidelines for farmers.
 
• **Species Exemptions:** Certain fast-growing or commercially valuable species are exempt from felling restrictions to promote economic activities.
 
• **Penalties for Non-Compliance:** Violating tree-felling rules can result in fines, penalties, and legal actions under environmental laws. 
 
• **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA):** Large-scale tree felling often requires an EIA to evaluate the ecological and social consequences.
